rows.b: Public patent CH705981A1 — -Low-pasta and to processes for their preparation.. Assignee: Dr Med Thomas Lacina. Class: A22
The correct answer attached to a training example, like the true next token.
A neural network trained on huge amounts of text so it can generate human-like writing, answer questions, and follow instructions.
How long you wait for an answer — the delay between asking and getting the first token back.
A step that rescales a layer's outputs to a steady range, keeping training stable and fast.
How big each parameter update is — too large and training blows up, too small and it crawls.
Gradually lowering the learning rate late in training so the model settles into its best settings.
A plan that changes the learning rate over time, usually warming up first and cooling down toward the end.
A lean C++ engine that runs quantized models on ordinary CPUs — the offline-everywhere workhorse.
Using a strong model to grade other models' answers, a fast stand-in for human raters.
The traffic cop spreading requests across many model servers.
Recording requests and outputs so problems can be diagnosed and behavior audited.
Manually boosting or suppressing specific tokens' scores to steer generation.
The raw, unnormalized scores the model produces for every vocabulary word before softmax turns them into probabilities.
The log-probability the model assigned to a token — the raw material of many evaluations.
Low-rank adaptation — fine-tuning by training tiny add-on matrices instead of the whole model, cheap and effective.
The score the training process tries to minimize, measuring how wrong the model's predictions are.
